big: A fund buys a bank's shares and sells another bank's futures, expecting the first to do better. It can gain even if the market falls. That is a long-short strategy, common in SIFs.

lines: How can a fund gain when prices fall?

By short exposure, taken through derivatives. A SIF may use it for a limited share of its net assets. An equity long-short fund holds shares and sells futures on weaker ones. And SIF strategies carry standard names so you know what you are buying.

rows: sell futures on shares expected to fall
note: Names such as equity long-short or debt long-short tell you what the fund does.
